title: Lensbridge: Side Accordion Orchestrator for Contextual Workspace Flows
creator: Aisha Fernando
description: Proposal for a compact, progressive side-accordion ‘Lensbridge’ that surfaces contextual workspace flows, rollouts, and cost lenses without fragmenting the primary canvas. The goal is to reduce cognitive overhead when switching contexts (project -> model -> route -> rollout) while preserving quick access to telemetry and cost breakdowns. This ticket drives a medium-fidelity prototype, engineering handoff notes, and a small moderated usability run focused on multi-workspace switching and canary rollout discovery.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates folding accordion regions that preserve last-read scroll position per workspace
Users can discover and open rollout lanes (canary / A-B / fallback) within two clicks from project header
Cost lens toggle is visible in the accordion header and shows token-level breakdown when expanded
Design tokens, spacing, and responsive collapse states documented for engineering
Engineering sign-off on CSS/ARIA approach for keyboard navigation and screen readers
tasks: Finalize accordion anatomy and responsive collapse breakpoints
Create mid-fi Figma flows (workspace switch, open rollout, toggle cost lens)
Prototype interactive state with keyboard traversal and opt-in compact mode
Run 6 moderated usability sessions and synthesize results
Prepare engineering handoff: redlines, interaction spec, accessibility notes
Sync with PM and Eng on routing semantics and persisted state storage
comments: 2026-02-13 - Aisha Fernando: Kickoff meeting — aligned on scope: navigation IA + rollout discovery + cost visibility. Agreed to preserve global header and avoid introducing new global modals.

2026-02-20 - Marco Li: Initial wireframes posted to Figma. Focus point: ensure that workspace-level pinned sections survive route transitions. Questioned storage: localStorage vs server-side preference for cross-device consistency.
2026-02-26 - PM review (Riley Thompson): Liked compact mode. Raised concern about default accordion state for org admins — recommend retention of expanded rollouts if user has active canaries.

2026-03-01 - Design critique: Accessibility gap called out — keyboard traversal between accordion headers required; outlined ARIA roles and focus ring specs. Also recommended visual weight reduction on non-active sections to reduce cognitive load.

2026-03-05 - Usability facilitator (Leah Park): Conducted 6 sessions (internal + 2 external customers). Findings summary: users preferred a contextual micro-summary in collapsed state (1-line: active rollouts + cost delta). Two users expected workspace switcher to remain at top of the accordion, so we iterated on persistent mini-chip placement.

2026-03-08 - Engineering feedback (Sanjay Rao): Backend prefers server-persisted accordion expansion state for enterprise customers. Raised performance question re: live token-level cost breakdowns; requested that the cost lens be lazy-loaded and cached for 60s.

2026-03-10 - Design update: Incorporated accessibility changes, added lazy-load pattern for cost lens, and included 3 variants for admin retention behavior (user preference, org policy, system default). Preparing final handoff package.
design_decisions: Persisted state: default to client-side for non-enterprise users; server-side opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers
Cost lens: lazy-load on expand, cache 60s, provide last-known snapshot in collapsed summary
Accessibility: accordion headers use button semantics with aria-expanded and aria-controls; arrow-key navigation between headers
Workspace switching: keep global quick-switcher in header; include workspace chips in accordion header for context
usability_summary: Participants: 6 (4 internal engineers, 2 product leads from customers)
Primary metrics: discoverability of rollout lanes (target: 90%), time-to-open-rollout (target: <4s), mental-model coherence for cost-lens (qualitative)
Outcome: rollout discovery achieved 83% (below target); two rapid iterations improved affordance by adding a micro-summary in collapsed state
Key quotes: 'I like that I can see if a canary exists before opening' — external PM; 'cost numbers need to be summarized, full breakdown only on demand' — internal engineer
next_steps: Create ENG spike to implement lazy-load endpoints and server-persisted state (ENG-54211)
Add admin policy toggle to console settings for retention behavior
Roll out design incrementally to 10% of orgs as an A/B test with telemetry on discovery and switch latency
Plan follow-up usability after the A/B window (2 weeks) to validate behaviour under real workloads
